The first four entries of both bias vectors share the same final two digits, which cannot happen by chance:

| index | b1 | b2 | last two digits |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.124 | 0.824 | 24 |
| 1 | 0.116 | 0.116 | 16 |
| 2 | 0.217 | -0.617 | 17 |
| 3 | -0.208 | 0.008 | 08 |

The leading digits differ, so the hider kept the original rough values and overwrote the hundredths and thousandths places with a letter index, writing the same code redundantly into b1 and b2. The remaining entries of both vectors do not match, so the message is exactly four symbols long.

Reading 24, 16, 17, 08 with the standard A=1 cipher gives X, P, Q, H. If the hider used A=0 instead, the same digits would read YQRI, but A=1 is the conventional letter-to-number mapping.

CODE: XPQH
